title: Architecture analysis: Build-time dependency installation with Docker layer caching
summary: Support build-time dependency installation via user-configured commands (e.g., `npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`) that run during `docker build` and are baked into the single `egg` image. The recommended approach dynamically generates per-repo COPY+RUN Dockerfile layers from `build_commands` config in `repositories.yaml`, maximizing Docker layer caching. This also fixes the existing `extra_packages` bug where config is inaccessible during build. Key design decisions include: running build commands as root in a staging directory (not the runtime repo path), failing the build on command failure, and documenting the volume-overlay limitation for local-installing package managers (npm) with a startup-copy workaround for advanced users.

problem_statement.description: In private mode, the sandbox container has no network access beyond the Anthropic API. Runtime dependency installation (`pip install`, `npm install`, `make deps`) fails. The existing `docker_setup.extra_packages` config only supports OS-level packages (apt/dnf) and is itself non-functional because `repositories.yaml` is not available in the Docker build context. There is no mechanism for running project-specific dependency installation commands at image build time with proper Docker layer caching.

root_causes.title: No build_commands config or execution path
root_causes.description: The config schema has no way to specify per-repo build commands. The Dockerfile and docker-setup.py only handle OS-level package installation via apt/dnf, not project-level dependency managers (pip, npm, go, cargo).

root_causes.title: Config inaccessible during Docker build
root_causes.description: create_dockerfile() at docker.py:210 does not copy repositories.yaml into the build context. During `docker build`, docker-setup.py's load_config() searches paths that don't exist inside the build environment (HOME is /root, no ~/repos/egg mount). This means extra_packages is silently ignored — a pre-existing bug.

root_causes.title: Build hash excludes dependency files
root_causes.description: compute_build_hash() at docker.py:417 hashes only egg source files (Dockerfile, scripts, shared modules). It does not include user dependency files (package-lock.json, requirements.txt), so changes to these files don't trigger image rebuilds.

root_causes.title: Volume overlay hides build-time local installs
root_causes.description: Local repos are volume-mounted at runtime at /home/egg/repos/<name> (compose.py:236), which overlays anything placed at those paths during build. Package managers that install locally (npm → node_modules/) lose their build-time artifacts at runtime. System-path installers (pip, go) are unaffected.

current_architecture.build_flow: The image build is orchestrated by sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py. build_image() calls should_rebuild_image() (compares SHA256 hash of all build files against label stored on image), then create_dockerfile() (copies egg source to ~/.cache/egg/ build context), then compute_build_hash(), then runs `docker build`. The Dockerfile is static — copied as-is from sandbox/Dockerfile to the build context.

key_components.name: build_image()
key_components.description: Entry point for image builds. Checks if rebuild needed, syncs build context, computes hash, runs docker build with build-args (USER_NAME, USER_UID, USER_GID, CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION) and label (org.egg.build-hash).

key_components.name: create_dockerfile()
key_components.description: Copies egg source files to ~/.cache/egg/ build context: docker-setup.py, claude-commands/, claude-rules/, runtime dirs (bin, egg_lib, llm, tools, scripts), shared/, pyproject.toml files, entrypoint.py, and the static Dockerfile.

key_components.name: compute_build_hash()
key_components.description: SHA256 hash of UID/GID, Dockerfile, entrypoint.py, docker-setup.py, pyproject.toml, and directories (claude-commands, claude-rules, bin, egg_lib, llm, tools, scripts, .claude/hooks, shared). Does NOT include user config or dependency files.

key_components.name: docker-setup.py
key_components.description: Runs during Docker build (Dockerfile line 59-63). Detects distro, loads config (unsuccessfully — bug), installs core packages (git, curl, build-essential, etc.) and user-configured extra packages. Config search: EGG_REPO_CONFIG env → ~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml → ~/repos/egg/config/repositories.yaml.

key_components.name: Dockerfile
key_components.description: Static Dockerfile: Ubuntu 22.04 → system packages → gh CLI → Python 3.11 → docker-setup.py (core/extra packages) → pip dependencies (base + private-mode pre-installs) → claude commands/rules → runtime scripts → git/gh gateway hijack → user creation → Claude Code CLI → entrypoint.

key_components.name: generate_compose_override()
key_components.description: Generates docker-compose.override.yml with per-repo volume mounts from local_repos.paths. Mounts each repo at /home/egg/repos/<name>. This is what causes the volume overlay that hides build-time local installs.

key_components.name: get_local_repos()
key_components.description: Loads local_repos.paths from repositories.yaml, resolves to absolute Path objects. Used by compose.py for volume mounts and will be needed by build_commands to locate watch files.

key_components.name: Config class
key_components.description: CONFIG_DIR = ~/.cache/egg/ (XDG-compliant). DOCKERFILE = CONFIG_DIR / 'Dockerfile'. IMAGE_NAME = 'egg'. This is the build staging directory.

key_components.name: repo_config.py
key_components.description: get_repo_setting(repo, setting, default) — generic per-repo config accessor. Loads from repo_settings in repositories.yaml with case-insensitive lookup.

approaches.title: Extend docker-setup.py with config in build context
approaches.description: Copy repositories.yaml (or a subset) into the build context. Extend docker-setup.py to read build_commands from config and execute them. Copy all watch files in a single COPY layer. Run all build commands in a single RUN layer via docker-setup.py.
pros: Minimal changes to the static Dockerfile (one new COPY + RUN layer)
Reuses existing config loading pattern in docker-setup.py
Fixes extra_packages bug as a side effect
Simple mental model — docker-setup.py handles all build-time setup
cons: Poor per-repo caching: one COPY layer for all watch files means any change rebuilds all repos' deps
Single RUN layer for all commands prevents independent caching
docker-setup.py becomes overloaded, mixing OS packages with project-level deps
Potentially copies sensitive data from repositories.yaml into the image (tokens are in secrets.env, but still a concern)

approaches.title: Dynamic Dockerfile generation with per-repo COPY+RUN layers
approaches.description: create_dockerfile() reads build_commands from config and appends per-repo COPY+RUN instructions to the static Dockerfile template. Each repo gets independent layers: COPY repo-deps/<name>/ /tmp/repo-deps/<name>/ then RUN cd /tmp/repo-deps/<name> && <commands>. Watch files are copied from local_repos.paths into the build context at repo-deps/<name>/.
pros: Optimal per-repo Docker layer caching — changing one repo's lockfile only rebuilds that repo's deps
Standard Docker best practice (COPY dependency files → RUN install before COPY source)
Clean separation — each repo's deps are independent layers
No config parsing at build time — commands are directly in Dockerfile
No sensitive config data in the image
cons: Shifts from static to dynamically generated Dockerfile
Dockerfile in build context diverges from what's in the repo — could confuse debugging
Must handle empty build_commands case (produce original static Dockerfile)
User-provided commands need careful shell escaping in generated RUN lines

approaches.title: Separate generated build script (minimal Dockerfile changes)
approaches.description: create_dockerfile() generates a build-deps.sh shell script embedding all repos' commands. The static Dockerfile gets two new lines: COPY build-deps.sh + RUN build-deps.sh. Watch files are still copied individually for each repo.
pros: No dynamic Dockerfile generation — only a generated shell script
Easy to debug (inspect build-deps.sh in the image)
cons: Same poor per-repo caching as Option A (single RUN layer for all repos)
Introduces new generated build artifact pattern
Must handle shell escaping of user-provided commands
Watch file changes still invalidate the single RUN layer for all repos

recommended_approach.title: Dynamic Dockerfile generation with per-repo COPY+RUN layers
recommended_approach.justification: The primary value of this feature is Docker layer caching — if deps haven't changed, skip reinstalling them. Option B maximizes this by giving each repo independent COPY+RUN layers, so changing one repo's lockfile doesn't invalidate another's dependency layer. This is the standard Docker pattern for dependency caching. The dynamic Dockerfile generation is a manageable complexity increase to create_dockerfile(), which already assembles a complex build context. The generated lines are simple string concatenation appended to the static template, keeping the core Dockerfile readable in the repo. Options A and C sacrifice per-repo caching (the core feature value) for marginal simplicity gains.
recommended_approach.risk_assessment: Low risk. The change is additive — repos without build_commands get the exact same static Dockerfile. Dynamic generation only appends lines. The static template in the repo remains the source of truth. All changes are in the host-side build tooling, not in the container runtime, so failures are caught at build time (not silently at runtime).

design_decisions.title: Volume overlay strategy for local-installing package managers
design_decisions.decision: Document the limitation and provide an opt-in startup-copy workaround
design_decisions.rationale: Package managers that install to local directories (npm → node_modules/, Bundler → vendor/bundle/) will have build-time installs hidden by runtime volume mounts. For MVP, document this as a known limitation and recommend: (a) use system-path installers when possible (pip installs globally as root, go modules use GOMODCACHE), (b) for npm, configure build_commands to install with `--prefix /opt/deps/<name>` and set NODE_PATH, or (c) use the `--global-style` npm flag. An opt-in `install_path` per-repo config can be added later for explicit staging + startup copy.
alternatives_considered: Automatic startup copy from staging path — adds startup latency, complex to implement correctly
Docker named volumes for node_modules — breaks the single-volume-per-repo model, complex compose generation
Overlay mounts (overlayfs) — requires privileged container, security concern

design_decisions.title: Build command execution context
design_decisions.decision: Run as root in /tmp/repo-deps/<name>/, the standard Docker build context
design_decisions.rationale: The Dockerfile runs all build steps as root before creating the egg user (line 147). Build commands should follow the same pattern. The working directory /tmp/repo-deps/<name>/ contains only the watch files. System-path installers (pip, go) install to global locations, which is the desired behavior. Commands that need specific user context can use `su -c`. Environment variables can be set via an optional `env` field in the config.
alternatives_considered: Run as egg user — egg user doesn't exist yet at the point where dep layers should be inserted (before line 147)
Run in /home/egg/repos/<name> — this path is overlaid by volume mounts at runtime; misleading

design_decisions.title: Build command failure handling
design_decisions.decision: Fail the Docker build on command failure (standard Docker behavior)
design_decisions.rationale: Build commands are user-configured for their specific projects. A failing command likely means broken dependencies, which would cause agent failures at runtime. Unlike extra_packages (which uses check=False for resilience against missing packages), build_commands represent explicit user intent — if `npm ci` fails, the image should not be built. Users can add `|| true` to individual commands if they want to ignore failures.
alternatives_considered: Log warning and continue (like extra_packages) — hides real failures, defeats the purpose of pre-installing deps
Per-command configurable — over-engineering for the MVP

design_decisions.title: Config accessibility fix for extra_packages
design_decisions.decision: Copy a minimal config subset into the build context alongside the build_commands fix
design_decisions.rationale: The existing extra_packages feature is non-functional because docker-setup.py can't find repositories.yaml during build. Rather than copying the full config (which could contain sensitive data), create_dockerfile() should extract the docker_setup section and write it as a minimal YAML file to the build context. This fixes the pre-existing bug and follows the principle of least privilege for build context data.
alternatives_considered: Copy full repositories.yaml — might contain sensitive per-repo settings
Embed extra_packages as build args — messy for complex package lists
Generate apt/dnf install commands directly in Dockerfile — duplicates docker-setup.py logic

design_decisions.title: Watch files to local_repos.paths mapping
design_decisions.decision: Use explicit repo-name matching between repo_settings keys and local_repos.paths basenames, with validation
design_decisions.rationale: The mapping between repo_settings keys (owner/repo format) and local_repos.paths (filesystem paths) is by directory basename matching the repo portion of the key. create_dockerfile() should: (1) parse the repo name from the settings key (e.g., 'web-app' from 'your-org/web-app'), (2) find the matching path in local_repos.paths by basename, (3) warn and skip if no matching local path exists (cloud-only repos can't have build_commands since there are no local files to copy). This uses the existing convention from compose.py.
alternatives_considered: Add explicit path mapping in config — adds complexity, redundant with local_repos.paths
Allow build_commands without local_repos — impossible since watch files must exist locally

design_decisions.title: Dockerfile generation strategy
design_decisions.decision: Append generated lines before the COPY . /opt/egg-runtime/ line (Dockerfile line 126)
design_decisions.rationale: Dependency installation layers should come after system packages and Python pip installs (so that system-level tools like gcc, make, node are available) but before the runtime scripts copy (so that runtime script changes don't invalidate dependency layers). The current Dockerfile has a natural insertion point: after the pip install blocks (line 104) and before the COPY . /opt/egg-runtime/ (line 126). create_dockerfile() reads the static Dockerfile, finds this insertion point, injects the per-repo COPY+RUN blocks, and writes the result.
alternatives_considered: Append at the end — runs after user creation, Claude Code install; deps would be cached poorly since user-creation layer changes with UID/GID
Insert before pip installs — pip might be needed by build commands (e.g., pip install -r requirements.txt)
Use Dockerfile ONBUILD — deprecated pattern, poor compatibility

tasks.title: Extend config schema with build_commands
tasks.description: Add `build_commands` section under `repo_settings` in the config schema. Structure: `build_commands: { watch_files: [str], commands: [str], env: {str: str} (optional) }`. Update `config/repositories.yaml.example` with documented examples. Add accessor functions to `config/repo_config.py`: `get_repo_build_commands(repo)` returning the build_commands dict, and `get_all_build_commands()` returning a dict of repo→build_commands for all repos with the setting.

tasks.title: Copy watch files into Docker build context
tasks.description: Extend `create_dockerfile()` in `docker.py` to: (1) load build_commands config for all repos, (2) resolve watch file paths by matching repo_settings keys to local_repos.paths basenames, (3) copy watch files from local repo paths into the build context at `~/.cache/egg/repo-deps/<repo-name>/`. Validate that watch files exist and warn if missing. Skip repos with no matching local path.

tasks.title: Generate per-repo Dockerfile layers
tasks.description: Extend `create_dockerfile()` to dynamically inject per-repo COPY+RUN instructions into the Dockerfile. Read the static Dockerfile template, find the insertion point (after pip installs, before COPY . /opt/egg-runtime/), and inject: `COPY repo-deps/<name>/ /tmp/repo-deps/<name>/` followed by `RUN cd /tmp/repo-deps/<name> && set -e && <cmd1> && <cmd2> ...` for each repo with build_commands. Handle shell escaping of user-provided commands. Write the modified Dockerfile to the build context.

tasks.title: Extend build hash to include watch files
tasks.description: Extend `compute_build_hash()` to include: (1) content of all watch files from all repos with build_commands, (2) the build_commands config itself (commands and env). This ensures that dependency file changes (e.g., updated package-lock.json) trigger image rebuilds, and command changes also trigger rebuilds.

tasks.title: Fix extra_packages config accessibility
tasks.description: In `create_dockerfile()`, extract the `docker_setup` section from repositories.yaml and write it as a minimal YAML file (`~/.cache/egg/sandbox/docker-setup-config.yaml`) in the build context. Update the Dockerfile's docker-setup.py COPY+RUN to also copy this config file. Update docker-setup.py's `load_config()` to check for the build-context config path (`/tmp/docker-setup-config.yaml`) as an additional search location.

tasks.title: Add tests for build_commands config and Dockerfile generation
tasks.description: Add unit tests for: (1) config accessor functions (get_repo_build_commands, get_all_build_commands), (2) watch file copying logic (matching repo names to local paths, handling missing files), (3) Dockerfile generation (correct insertion point, proper escaping, empty build_commands produces unchanged Dockerfile), (4) build hash includes watch file contents. Extend existing test_docker.py and test_docker_setup.py.

tasks.title: Update documentation
tasks.description: Update: (1) config/repositories.yaml.example with build_commands examples (covered by task-1), (2) sandbox/README.md with build_commands documentation including the volume overlay limitation and workarounds, (3) config/README.md if it references docker_setup.

implementation_plan.ordering: Tasks 1 and 5 can be done in parallel (independent). Tasks 2-3 depend on task 1 (config accessors needed). Task 4 depends on task 1. Task 6 depends on all implementation tasks. Task 7 depends on implementation being stable.
implementation_plan.critical_path: task-1 → task-2 → task-3 (config → watch files → Dockerfile generation)

constraints: Single image — all repos' dependencies must coexist in one `egg` image, no per-repo images
Volume overlay — runtime volume mounts at /home/egg/repos/<name> hide build-time contents at those paths
No full repo at build time — only watch files are available; full repos are mounted at runtime
Backwards compatible — repos without build_commands must produce the exact same Dockerfile and image
Static Dockerfile remains in repo — dynamic generation only in the build context copy, not the source
Build hash must include watch file contents to trigger rebuilds on dependency changes
Docker layer caching order — dependency COPY+RUN must come after system tool installs but before frequently-changing layers
Private mode primary use case — no network at runtime, deps must be pre-installed in the image

internal: sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py — main build orchestration (create_dockerfile, compute_build_hash, build_image)
sandbox/egg_lib/config.py — get_local_repos() for resolving repo paths
sandbox/egg_lib/compose.py — volume mount generation (not modified, but constrains design)
external: Docker BuildKit layer caching — per-repo COPY+RUN caching behavior

open_questions.title: Environment variable support for build commands
open_questions.description: Should the config support an optional `env` map for setting environment variables during build commands? Examples: NODE_ENV=production, PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1, GOPATH=/opt/go. The proposed schema includes this as optional, but it could be deferred to a follow-up if not needed for MVP.
open_questions.recommendation: Include env support in the schema but make it optional. Implementation is trivial (add ENV lines before RUN in generated Dockerfile). Defer if it adds scope.

open_questions.title: Dockerfile insertion point marker
open_questions.description: The dynamic generation inserts lines at a specific point in the Dockerfile. Should we add a comment marker (e.g., `# === BUILD_COMMANDS_INSERT_POINT ===`) to make the insertion point explicit, or rely on content matching (e.g., find the 'COPY . /opt/egg-runtime/' line)?
open_questions.recommendation: Use a comment marker. It's explicit, resilient to Dockerfile refactoring, and self-documenting. Add `# === DEPENDENCY_LAYERS ===` as a marker in the static Dockerfile.

open_questions.title: Forced rebuild of dependency layers
open_questions.description: Should there be a `--rebuild-deps` flag (separate from --rebuild) to force rebuild only the dependency layers without rebuilding the entire image?
open_questions.recommendation: Defer. The existing `--rebuild` flag (which does --no-cache) is sufficient for now. Per-layer cache invalidation would require BuildKit cache mounts, which is a larger change.
